_readme: Job-type catalogue used by make_jobs.py to build data/jobs.json for the whole demand period.
Edit the numbers here, then run: python make_jobs.py
Every number has a 'source'. ASSUMPTION = our own choice, replace it when you have a measured value.
power_kw of a task = gpus x hardware.kw_per_gpu (GPU board power + share of the host server).

hardware.gpu_board_w_source: NVIDIA L4 Tensor Core GPU datasheet: max thermal design power 72 W. MLPerf Inference v6.1 summary.xlsx (data/sources) has throughput only, no power measurements, so the datasheet value is used.
hardware.host_w_per_gpu_source: ASSUMPTION: CPU, memory, disks and fans of a 4-GPU host (~200 W) shared over its 4 GPUs. Replace with a wall-plug measurement of your server.

arrival_profile.source: Alibaba cluster-trace-gpu-v2020, pai_task_table: share of 732,691 completed GPU tasks started in each hour of the day (68 days, July-Aug 2020). The trace keeps time of day but shifts timestamps by a constant, so the hours are in the trace's own time zone (likely UTC+8). The profile is fairly flat: 2.8 % to 6.9 % per hour.

trace_facts._note: Computed from data/sources/pai_task_table.csv (completed tasks with a GPU request); used to choose the job types below.
trace_facts.repeated_instances: 68.7 % of instances belong to a group that repeats 5 or more times (pai_group_tag_table) -> jobs repeating every day is realistic

prices.usd_to_chf_source: ASSUMPTION: set the current exchange rate.
prices.gpu_hour_source: AWS g6.xlarge (1x NVIDIA L4), eu-central-1 Frankfurt: on-demand ~1.0064 USD/h (aws-pricing.com), spot ~0.356 USD/h lowest AZ (doit.com). Zurich eu-central-2: 1.085 / 0.337 USD/h (devzero.io). Third-party trackers, retrieved 2026-11-21.
prices.priority_price_source: ASSUMPTION: critical work is sold at on-demand price, flexible at spot price, normal in between.

job_types.name: Transcribe call recordings
job_types.source: Inference job (Whisper-type speech model; Whisper is an MLPerf Inference v6.1 benchmark). One full GPU like 45.5 % of trace tasks; 60 min is above the trace median for inference GPUs (T4: 5.7 min, p90 119 min) because a batch of recordings is bundled. Deadline and volume: ASSUMPTION.

job_types.name: Retrain recommendation (CTR) model
job_types.source: 'ctr' is the 2nd most common workload tag (26 % of tagged instances). 120 min sits between the trace p75 (63 min) and p90 (212 min). Deadline (ready next morning) and volume: ASSUMPTION.

job_types.name: Embed document archive (BERT)
job_types.source: 'bert' is the most common workload tag (53 % of tagged instances). Half a GPU like 15.8 % of trace tasks (26-50 % GPU request). 30 min batches ~ trace p50-p75. Merge waits for all batches. Volume: ASSUMPTION.

job_types.name: Fine-tune language model (NMT/BERT)
job_types.source: Long training tasks carry most GPU time in the trace: tasks of 8 h or more hold 61 % of GPU-hours. 4 workers + an evaluator follows the trace's worker/evaluator roles. Checkpointed, so interruptible. Deadline and volume: ASSUMPTION.

job_types.name: Hyper-parameter sweep
job_types.source: Short tasks on a GPU share: 36.2 % of trace tasks request 25 % of a GPU or less; trace median duration 10 min (rounded up to one 15-min slot). Volume: ASSUMPTION.
